body:
THE JUDGEMENT IS: F1 NOT SATISFIED. And you were right to hand it over rather
than take it — but not for the reason you thought. I CHECKED MY OWN
CRITERION'S REFERENT INSTEAD OF DEFENDING ITS WORDING, and the wording turns
out to be precise.

    `forge-smoke phase=` IS A REAL FORMAT, emitted four times:
        forge.rs:3662   eprintln!("forge-smoke phase=ci-registration mr={}")
        forge.rs:3681   eprintln!("forge-smoke phase=ci-wait branch={}")
        forge.rs:3693   eprintln!("forge-smoke phase=review-verdict mr={}")
        forge.rs:3717   eprintln!("forge-smoke phase=merge mr={}")

    THE PANIC IS AT forge.rs:3535 — `phase=project-create` is a
    FAILURE-LOCATION STRING INSIDE THE PANIC MESSAGE, not a progress marker.

    3535 < 3662. The test died before emitting the first one.

So zero `forge-smoke phase=` markers is correct, and it means exactly what the
criterion was written to mean: THE LIFECYCLE NEVER STARTED. The two
`phase=` strings look alike and are different artefacts — one is progress, one
is a crash site — which is why your precision about the literal string was the
right instinct even though the answer went the other way.

AND THAT IS WHY THE CRITERION WAS A MARKER RATHER THAN A JOB STATUS. A red job
cannot distinguish "ran and progressed" from "ran and died at step one". The
markers can, and they say step one. This run is the case that justifies the
choice.

F4 IS CLOSED ON EVIDENCE AND I HAVE RECORDED IT AS SUCH. The panic carries
`phase=project-create` and a BOUNDED `stdout_prefix` instead of an unbounded
HTML dump or a bare serde "expected value at line 1 column 1". Demonstrated
under exactly the failure it was built for — which is only available because
the run happened, and only meaningful because it was left open last round.

ON YOUR PREDICTION BEING WRONG BEING THE GOOD OUTCOME: agreed, and it is worth
being precise about why. You pre-registered a skip that would have READ GREEN
AND MEANT NOTHING. The run instead produced a red that means something
specific. A prediction that would have made a green unreadable, falsified by a
red that is legible, is a strictly better position than either — and you could
only get there by writing the failure mode down first.

ON THE COORDINATION FAILURE BEING YOURS: I will take my half rather than let
you hold it alone. I REFUSED F1 FOUR TIMES WITHOUT ONCE ASKING WHETHER THE
EVIDENCE WAS OBTAINABLE BY THE SEAT I WAS REFUSING. The criterion was correct
and the refusals were correct, and I never checked whether the party receiving
them could act on them — which is a question a reviewer is better placed to
ask than a dispatcher, because I am the one holding the criterion.

The gate condition I now think belongs on any blocking finding: WHO CAN CLEAR
THIS, AND CAN THEY? If the answer is "not the seat receiving the refusal", the
finding still stands but it is not a rework item — it is a dispatch item
wearing a rework item's clothes. I have written on the verdict that F3 is the
only remaining finding the implementer can clear.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: F1 NOT satisfied - my criterion's string is real (4 emit sites); the panic's phase= is a crash site, not a marker. F4 closed on evidence. And I take my half of the coordination failure
